title: Evaluate your data agent - Microsoft Fabric | Microsoft Learn
summary: Microsoft Learn's how-to for the (preview) Fabric Data Agent Python SDK evaluation workflow: installing the SDK, loading a ground-truth question/expected-answer dataset, running evaluate_data_agent, and inspecting summary and row-level results, plus how to swap in a custom LLM-as-judge critic prompt and use the Diagnostics export for troubleshooting.
audience: Data scientists and platform engineers who need to regression-test a data agent's accuracy programmatically before promoting it to production, rather than manually clicking through the chat UI.
why_it_matters: Because a data agent's behavior depends on instructions, example queries, and an underlying LLM rather than fixed logic, its accuracy can drift as any of those change; a notebook-driven evaluation loop with a swappable judging prompt is what makes that accuracy measurable and repeatable instead of anecdotal.
takeaways: Evaluation is a preview, notebook-based workflow built on a pip-installable SDK (fabric-data-agent-sdk), not a UI feature.
The core loop is: build a question/expected_answer dataset (DataFrame or CSV), call evaluate_data_agent, then pull a summary or row-level detail table.
Each run writes two Fabric tables — a summary table and a '_steps' table with full reasoning traces — rather than just returning an in-memory result.
Matching is done by an LLM-as-judge critic prompt that is fully replaceable, which matters when expected answers vary in formatting but are still semantically correct.
The same Diagnostics export used for evaluation troubleshooting is also the mechanism recommended for engaging Microsoft Support.

claims.text: Programmatic evaluation of a Fabric data agent is a preview capability delivered through a separate pip-installable package, fabric-data-agent-sdk, run from a Fabric notebook rather than the chat UI.

Evaluation shares the same capacity and tenant prerequisites as building a data agent: a paid F2+ or P1+ capacity with Fabric enabled, plus the tenant's cross-geo processing/storing for AI setting turned on.

A ground-truth evaluation set is a simple two-column table of question and expected_answer pairs, supplied either as an in-notebook pandas DataFrame or loaded from a CSV file with those exact column names.

The evaluate_data_agent function runs the ground-truth question set against a named data agent (targeting either its production or sandbox stage) and returns a unique evaluation_id while writing results into a summary table plus a same-named '_steps' table holding detailed reasoning and execution traces.
get_evaluation_summary reads back an evaluation's aggregated metrics — total questions evaluated, counts of true/false/unclear results, and overall accuracy — from the evaluation output table.

get_evaluation_details returns row-level results for a specific evaluation run — question, expected answer, actual answer, a true/false/unclear evaluation_result, and a thread_url — and can be filtered to only the failing or unclear rows instead of the full set.

Whether an actual answer counts as matching the expected answer is judged by an LLM using a built-in critic prompt by default, and this prompt can be fully replaced via a critic_prompt parameter that must include {query}, {expected_answer}, and {actual_answer} placeholders.

A custom critic prompt is useful for loosening or tightening the match criteria and for handling cases where expected and actual answers differ in formatting but are semantically equivalent or involve domain-specific judgment.
The evaluation thread_url returned in row-level detail results is only accessible to the user who ran that evaluation, not to other collaborators.

The Diagnostics button exports a full snapshot of a data agent's configuration and execution steps — including data source settings, applied instructions, and example queries used — for troubleshooting or for engaging Microsoft Support.
